VAL-ISSUE-001.summary: Issue assignment creates one Droid task even from non-default issue states.

VAL-ISSUE-002.summary: Directed member comments and assignee-addressed replies retrigger Droid and keep output anchored to the relevant thread root.

VAL-ISSUE-003.summary: Broadcasts, member-only replies, and comments directed elsewhere do not auto-trigger Droid.

VAL-ISSUE-004.summary: Explicit Droid mentions still trigger work on unassigned or terminal issues.

VAL-ISSUE-005.summary: Plain follow-up replies inherit the root Droid mention exactly in the supported cases and do not misfire when redirected elsewhere.

VAL-ISSUE-006.summary: Assignment-originated completion output appears exactly once in visible issue history.

VAL-ISSUE-007.summary: Reassignment visibly supersedes the old run, leaves one cancellation marker, and routes exactly one replacement task.

VAL-ISSUE-008.summary: Blocked, failed, cancelled, and superseded issue runs keep durable, distinguishable history and transcript metadata.

VAL-CHAT-001.summary: Users can start a chat session with a Droid-backed agent as a first-class conversation.

VAL-CHAT-002.summary: The first chat message creates one persisted user message, one task binding, and the expected pending task state.

VAL-CHAT-003.summary: The live chat flow continued to expose Droid execution activity during the validated two-turn browser flow, with chat state helpers preserving the active task marker logic.

VAL-CHAT-004.summary: Completed Droid replies persist, clear pending state, and remain reload-stable with the original agent identity.

VAL-CHAT-005.summary: A second turn stays in the same persisted Droid chat session and preserves prior context.

VAL-CHAT-006.summary: Archived sessions remain readable, keep history intact, and reject new sends without silently spawning new work.

VAL-CHAT-007.summary: Failed or cancelled chat turns clear live state, leave a durable failure marker, and do not fabricate assistant replies.

VAL-CHAT-008.summary: A first-turn send failure leaves no orphaned normal message: the denied archived-agent session has zero persisted messages after rejection.

VAL-CROSS-001.summary: The same Droid runtime was used to create a Droid agent that immediately executed assignment-created work without operator-only steps.

VAL-CROSS-002.summary: Assignment and explicit mention both produce inspectable Droid task provenance with stable agent and runtime metadata.

VAL-CROSS-003.summary: Assignment and chat entry points enforce the same availability and permission rules for Droid agents.

VAL-CROSS-004.summary: Droid-authored results remain first-class across issue comments, chat replies, and transcript/history surfaces.

VAL-CROSS-005.summary: Private Droid agents deny both assignment and chat for non-owners while allowing both for the owner.

VAL-CROSS-006.summary: Archived Droid agents stop new assignment and chat work while preserving readable issue, chat, and transcript history.
